question: Aarti, Anil and Naveen started a business in partnership, investing in the ratio of 17:6:17, respectively. At the end of the year, they earned a profit of ₹78,600, which is 20% of their total investment. How much did Anil invest (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 20% of total investment → Total investment = 78600 ÷ 0.2 = 393000

Ratio sum = 17 + 6 + 17 = 40

Anil’s share = 6/40 of total

= (6/40) × 393000 = 58950

**∴ Answer = ₹58950**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio = 17 : 6 : 17, Profit = 78600, Profit = 20% of total investment

**Formula used:**

Total Investment = Profit × (100/Percentage)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total investment = 78600 × (100/20) = 78600 × 5 = 393000

⇒ Total ratio = 17 + 6 + 17 = 40

⇒ Value of 1 part = 393000 ÷ 40 = 9825

⇒ Anil’s investment = 6 × 9825 = 58950

**∴ The correct answer is ₹58950.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Ratio

Investment ratio determines profit share if time is same.

Percentage Conversion

20% = 1/5 → Total = 5 × profit

Unitary Method

Find value of 1 part, then multiply by required ratio.

Equal Time Rule

If duration is same, profit ∝ investment.
